title: Script is non-idempotent with no progress/checkpoint guard — a re-run redeploys everything, re-revokes/re-grants phUSD mint, overwrites the handoff JSON, producing a recoverable split-brain across the saga (operator footgun)
description: The script has no idempotency / checkpoint guard. A re-run (e.g. after a partial failure or ambiguity) redeploys everything, re-revokes/re-grants phUSD mint, and overwrites the handoff JSON, producing a recoverable split-brain: a second minterV2/strategies set is granted mint authority while addresses.ts and 2.2/2.3 still reference the first deployment. This departs from the project's own documented checkpoint/resilient-deployment pattern. Per-entryPoint fingerprint correctly prevents suppression by the superseded YS-35 route (saga-2.1 replaces that route).
impact: No direct asset loss; the split-brain is explicitly RECOVERABLE — the orphaned second minterV2 holds no user funds and is not wired into the staker. Bites only on an operator re-run during the migration window. C4 Low/QA (closest-to-line Low: would be Medium only if a re-run could irrecoverably grant mint to an attacker-influenced address or strand user funds — neither is the case).
attackPath: Operator re-runs 2.1 (e.g. after a partial failure or ambiguity).
Script redeploys contracts, re-grants mint authority, overwrites the handoff JSON.
addresses.ts / 2.2 / 2.3 still reference the first deployment -> split-brain across the saga during the most fragile window.
recommendation: Add an idempotency/checkpoint guard before redeploying or re-granting mint: detect an existing 2.1 deployment (from the handoff JSON / on-chain markers) and skip-or-resume rather than blindly redeploying, matching the project's documented resilient-deployment pattern.

evidence.observed: Unconditional deploy + re-grant + handoff JSON overwrite on every run; no checkpoint guard.
evidence.recoverable: Orphaned second minterV2 holds no user funds, not wired into the staker.
evidence.suppressionBoundary: Lineage to the superseded YS-35 route does not suppress — per-entryPoint fingerprint; saga-2.1 replaces that route.

footgunRationale: Non-obvious operator footgun (Law 3): a re-run silently creating a split-brain is surprising. In scope as an operational hazard; safe-config guidance: add an idempotency/checkpoint guard before redeploying or re-granting mint.
